diffs.diff: pin count: part has 4 (GND DT SCK VCC), datasheet reading has 10 (GND DT SCK VCC E+ E- A- A+ B- B+)
diffs.evidence: The vendor pinout for this exact green module shows two separate headers: J1 (load-cell side) E+, E-, A-, A+, B-, B+ and J2 (microcontroller side) GND, DT, SCK, VCC. The part models the module sold together with its 5 kg bar load cell, so J1 is occupied by the included cell (red E+, black E-, white A-, green A+, as stated in the part description and build notes) and B-/B+ are unused; the only pins a user wires to the ESP32/Pico are J2's 4 pins, in the order GND, DT, SCK, VCC, which match the part exactly. The second reading counted both headers as one 10-pin header.

diffs.diff: differential input voltage (V), channel A gain 128, AVDD=5V: datasheet reading gives 2.384185791015625e-9 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Datasheet: 'Full-scale differential input range V(inp)-V(inn): ±0.5(AVDD/GAIN) V' and 'Output data coding 2's complement 800000 .. 7FFFFF HEX'; 'Channel A ... gain of 128 or 64, corresponding to a full-scale differential input voltage of ±20mV or ±40mV respectively, when a 5V supply is connected to AVDD'. The second reading used the rounded ±20 mV (20 mV / 2^23 = 2.384e-9 V/count); the exact table value is 0.5*5/128 = 19.53 mV / 2^23 = 2.328e-9 V/count (2.4% different). The part does not expose a raw voltage: its sim (kind hx711, countsPerUnit 429.4967296 counts/g) expresses the same datasheet relation in grams for the bundled 1 mV/V, 5 kg cell excited ratiometrically from AVDD: 2^23 counts / (0.5*AVDD/128) * (1e-3*AVDD/5000 g) = 2^31*1e-3/5000 = 429.4967 counts/g, independent of AVDD. So the model is consistent with the exact datasheet formula; the comparator just cannot see a counts-per-gram constant.
